summary: EmbeddedGateway (embedded_gateway.jac + embedded_gateway.impl.jac) and InProcessTransport (in transport/transport.jac) form an in-process gateway path with no production caller. Grepped `EmbeddedGateway` and `InProcessTransport` across every .jac file in the repo: the only hits outside their own definitions are tests/microservices/test_embedded_gateway.jac and test_runtime_integration.jac. planner.jac computes a gateway_mode of 'embedded' vs 'process', but its only production consumer, local_realizer.jac, merely logs plan.gateway_mode in an f-string and never branches on it. orchestrator.jac (the real production entry point invoked from plugin.jac) unconditionally constructs ProcessGateway regardless of topology, and plugin.jac itself has zero references to 'embedded' anywhere. This is a fully-built, fully-tested, never-wired subsystem safe to delete along with its dedicated test file.

This ~492-line file defines JacScalePluginConfig, a static schema/metadata-description class (get_plugin_metadata, get_config_schema) that re-describes every default already declared in config/impl/config_loader.impl.jac's get_default_config(), as a verbose nested dict. Grepped the whole repo for JacScalePluginConfig and found only its own declaration line — nothing imports, instantiates, or calls its static methods, including its own test suite. Sibling plugin-config classes elsewhere in the monorepo (JacMcpPluginConfig, byllm's) are exercised by jac/tests/cli/test_mcp.jac; this one has zero references anywhere. Entire file can be deleted.

This entire ~55-line file defines three free functions (_transport_response_to_dict, _get_http_status, _transport_response_to_json_response) that convert a TransportResponse into a JSONResponse. Grepped the whole repo for both function names: the only hits are their own definitions in this file — no caller anywhere, and the functions aren't tied to any declared archetype via `impl X.Y` so nothing forward-declares them either. The functionally identical conversion is actually wired in via jserver/impl/jfast_api.impl.jac's `_convert_transport_response_to_json_response`, called 8 times inside JFastApiServer._create_endpoint_function — confirmed by reading both files in full and comparing the dict-shape logic (ok/type/data/error/meta handling is the same). The whole file is a safe, straightforward deletion.

Gateway is an abstract base declaring a middleware field and setup()/serve() stubs. Only two classes ever extend it: EmbeddedGateway (confirmed dead in a separate finding) and ProcessGateway. Grepped `self\.middleware` repo-wide: ProcessGateway.setup()/.serve() never reference it (the only non-gateway.jac hit is inside the dead embedded_gateway.impl.jac). ProcessGateway itself does nothing but construct an internal MicroserviceGateway with the same constructor args and forward .serve() to .start(). MicroserviceGateway — the class that does all real routing/admin-API/tracing/metrics/middleware work — does not inherit Gateway at all. With EmbeddedGateway dead, the interface has exactly one live implementation that is a pure pass-through wrapper; orchestrator.jac could construct MicroserviceGateway directly and both gateway.jac and process_gateway.jac could be deleted.

MiddlewareRegistry.run()/_invoke() hand-roll a recursive call-next middleware chain. Grepped `\.run\(request|registry\.run\(` repo-wide: the only callers are in test_middleware.jac and test_runtime_integration.jac. Every production caller — microservice_gateway.impl.jac (the real gateway) and the dead embedded_gateway.impl.jac — only calls `self.middleware.install(app)`, which registers each Middleware.handle directly via `app.add_middleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware, dispatch=middleware.handle)` and lets Starlette do the onion-chaining itself. The hand-rolled _invoke(index, request, handler) chain duplicates what add_middleware already does and is exercised only by unit tests calling run() directly instead of going through install().

JacAPIServerCore.start calls _find_available_port(self.port) (a pre-flight test-socket bind loop) before starting the server when there's no prebound listen socket, then calls self.server.run_server(port=self.port). But JFastApiServer.run_server (jfast_api.impl.jac, lines ~151-188) has its own independent retry loop that catches SystemExit/OSError 'Address already in use' from uvicorn.Server.run() and increments the port itself, for the same non-prebound code path. Because the pre-check releases its test socket before uvicorn binds, it doesn't even eliminate the race that run_server's own retry loop exists to handle, so run_server's loop does the real work regardless — confirmed by reading both retry implementations in full. The pre-check's only unique value (an early console message) could be produced from inside run_server's existing loop instead.

summary: The entire 169-line file defines `JacByllmPluginConfig` with `get_plugin_metadata()`/`get_config_schema()` static methods, but nothing in the repo calls either method on this class. Grepped the whole repo for `JacByllmPluginConfig` (case-sensitive) and the only hit is the definition itself; grepped for `.get_config_schema(` and `.get_plugin_metadata(` repo-wide and every call site targets a different module's sibling class (`JacMcpPluginConfig` in `jac/tests/cli/test_mcp.jac`) — byllm's own class has zero callers, including in its own tests. Actual byllm config plumbing goes through the entirely separate `JacByllmConfig`/`get_byllm_config()` in `config_loader.jac` + `impl/config_loader.impl.jac`, which is what every runtime call site (`llm.jac`, `basellm.impl.jac`, `mtir.impl.jac`, `cli/impl/ai_agent.impl.jac`, etc.) actually imports and uses. Confirming this is stale, not just unwired: the hand-written schema in this dead file omits several sections that exist in the real, live `get_default_config()` (`parallel`, `streaming`, `fallback`, and most of `compaction`/`local`), proving nobody has kept it in sync because nothing reads it. It is nonetheless actively harmful: `jac/jaclang/publish/runtime_vendor.jac` lists `"jaclang.byllm.plugin_config"` in `_BYLLM_SEEDS`, so this dead module and its stale schema dict get vendored into every published/ejected byllm app for no functional benefit.

`BaseLLM.dispatch_no_streaming` (lines 1163-1189) and `BaseLLM.adispatch_no_streaming` (lines 1368-1390) contain a word-for-word identical ~26-line block: extract `message` from the response, run `recover_tool_calls`/`_sanitize_tool_calls`, `mt_run.add_message(message)`, compute `output_content`, `finish_reason`, `truncated_ids`, `tool_calls`, `output_value`, and build the returned `CompletionResult`. I diffed the two blocks line by line and they are identical except for one added `self.log_info` call in the sync variant. `dispatch_streaming_with_tools` (lines 1318-1339) contains the same core tail (`_sanitize_tool_calls` through the final `CompletionResult`/append) with only the tool-recovery pre-check differing. None of this logic touches `await`/generators — it's pure post-processing of an already-obtained `response`/`message`, so it is safe to extract into one shared helper (e.g. `_finalize_completion(self, mt_run, message, usage_data, log=True)`) called from all three sites instead of copy-pasted.

The context-window override resolution block is copy-pasted verbatim across three `_get_ctx_window` overrides: `BaseLLM._get_ctx_window` (basellm.impl.jac:219-230), `LocalLLM._get_ctx_window` (llm.impl/local.impl.jac:103-115, which inserts one extra `or int(self.config.get("n_ctx", 0))` fallback), and `ModelPool._get_ctx_window` (llm.impl/modelpool.impl.jac:84-102). I read all three implementations in full and confirmed the first 7 lines (the `override = int(...)`/`if override > 0 { return override; }` guard) are identical in `BaseLLM` and `ModelPool`, and near-identical in `LocalLLM`; only the final fallback (`_litellm_ctx_window`, `self.spec.get("n_ctx", 4096)`, or `min(windows)` across pooled models) differs. Since `Model.invoke` already calls `super.invoke(mt_run)` elsewhere in this codebase (llm.impl/model.impl.jac:75), `super._get_ctx_window(call_params)` is a proven-working pattern here too — `LocalLLM`/`ModelPool` could call `super._get_ctx_window(call_params)` and only add their own fallback when the base returns 0, eliminating two of the three copies of the override block.

`model_cache.jac` defines `_fmt_size(mb)` (lines 49-54, MB-in/GB-or-MB-out) purely for the local-model-download UX, while `cli.jac` defines a second, independent human-readable size formatter `_human_bytes(n)` (lines 9-18, bytes-in, walks B/KB/MB/GB/TB). Grepped both files and confirmed each is only called within its own file (`_fmt_size` at model_cache.jac:75 and :113-115; `_human_bytes` at cli.jac:42) — they never call each other, and `cli.jac`'s `_cmd_model` `list` action even has a third, unformatted ad-hoc case (`f"~{int(spec.get('size_mb', 0))} MB"` at cli.jac:44) for not-yet-downloaded entries instead of reusing either helper. All three exist to solve the exact same 'show a human-friendly model size' problem for the same feature (`jac model list/pull`). Since `_human_bytes` already handles the full unit range, `_fmt_size` and the inline MB literal could both be replaced with a single call to `_human_bytes(mb * 1024 * 1024)`, removing one hand-rolled formatter and the inline special case.
